# Candidate findings for outreach

Three one-sentence findings about **method**, not about injected error rates. Every number comes from `outputs/summary.json`, which is built from the output files named under each finding. All data is synthetic and all dollar figures are estimates.

## 1. A careful baseline's duplicate flags were mostly false, and the cause was a missing business rule

> A careful spreadsheet baseline flagged {{baseline_duplicates.flags|int}} duplicate invoices and {{baseline_duplicates.false_share|pct0}} of them were wrong; {{baseline_duplicates.share_explained_by_rebills_and_balance_due|pct0}} of the wrong ones were rebills or balance-due invoices, which legitimately repeat the original invoice's BOL and which a BOL-only match cannot tell from a resend.

- Numbers: {{baseline_duplicates.false_flags|int}} false duplicate flags out of {{baseline_duplicates.flags|int}} ({{baseline_duplicates.false_share|pct}}); {{baseline_duplicates.false_from_rebills|int}} on rebill invoices and {{baseline_duplicates.false_from_balance_due|int}} on balance-due invoices. The engine, which links a rebill to the invoice it replaces and treats a balance-due invoice as a different charge, raised {{engine_vs_baseline.by_type.duplicate_invoice.engine.fp|int}} false duplicate flags.
- Sources: `outputs/eval_by_type.csv` (duplicate_invoice rows), `outputs/baseline_fp_causes.csv` (the rebill / balance due cause).
- Caveat: the baseline is deliberately given no supersession logic; the finding is about which rule closes the gap, not about spreadsheets being bad.

## 2. A peer-rate test turns many separate fuel flags into one carrier-level escalation

> {{systemic.strongest.carrier_name}}'s fuel surcharge was overbilled by only about {{systemic.strongest.mean_flag_dollars_estimate|usd}} (estimate) on a typical flagged invoice, yet a one-sided binomial test against the other {{systemic.strongest.mode}} carriers showed {{systemic.strongest.flagged|int}} of {{systemic.strongest.invoices|int}} invoices flagged in {{systemic.strongest.window_start|month}} to {{systemic.strongest.window_end|month}} ({{systemic.strongest.carrier_rate|pct}} against {{systemic.strongest.other_carriers_rate|pct}}, p = {{systemic.strongest.p_value|p}}), which points to one wrong fuel table and not {{systemic.strongest.flagged|int}} separate mistakes.

- Numbers: billed {{systemic.strongest.avg_billed_over_expected|pct}} above expected on average; significance threshold after Bonferroni correction {{systemic.strongest.alpha_adjusted|p}}.
- Sources: `outputs/systemic_findings.csv`, `outputs/audit_flags.csv` (the mean flagged dollars).
- Caveat: the same test also flagged {{systemic.n_others}} weaker pattern ({{systemic.others.0.carrier_name}}, {{systemic.others.0.error_type}}, p = {{systemic.others.0.p_value|p}} against a threshold of {{systemic.others.0.alpha_adjusted|p}}) that was not planted, so a finding is a reason to ask the carrier, not proof.

## 3. Accessorials are a small part of accrued dollars and most of the accrual error, and late authorizations explain much of it

> Month-end accruals landed {{accruals.net_error_pct_estimate|abspct2}} {{accruals.direction}} eventual payable overall, but accessorials were only {{accruals.accessorial_share_of_accrual|pct}} of accrued dollars and {{accruals.accessorial_share_of_net_error|pct0}} of the net {{accruals.gap_word}}, and {{accruals.late_authorization_share_of_net_error|pct0}} of the net {{accruals.gap_word}} came from authorizations recorded after month-end, which an accrual cannot use.

- Numbers: net {{accruals.gap_word}} {{accruals.net_error_estimate|absusd}} on accruals of {{accruals.accrual_estimate|usd}} (estimates); mean absolute monthly error {{accruals.mape_pct_estimate|pct2}}; recording every authorization at delivery would have moved the accrual by {{accruals.late_authorization_effect_estimate|usd}} (estimate) and left the overall error at {{accruals.net_error_pct_if_authorized_at_delivery_estimate|abspct2}} {{accruals.direction}} payable.
- Sources: `outputs/accrual_accuracy.csv` (ALL row), `outputs/accrual_sensitivity.csv` (ALL row).
- Caveat: shares are of the net signed error over the whole period, so months of opposite sign offset each other; the share of late authorizations is set by `accessorials.late_authorization_share` in the config.
